body:
While this was the original idea with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115926 it wasn't a good idea. Adding more properties to CSG nodes is limited, the correct solution is to implement a face editor.
I abandoned that PR because I started working on something that would be better at solving the problem, the ability to edit `CSGBrush`es and the possibility of making a face editor https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118630

This PR introduces tools that would be redundant if mine was merged, as mine already provides a way to generate cube and cylinder UVs, not just for Box and Cylinder but for any CSG node in local and global space. It also allows changing material per face and other properties of face, as well as rotating, scaling, translating and mirroring UVs.
And the ability to edit the brush while transforming the scale of UVs could be implemented through a toggle in the toolbar to make it recalculate UVs while editing.

-----

I think there is some use for `CSGPolygon3D` having better UVs since the shapes that can be created are more complex, and that part of the PR is pretty cool, but the other shapes should remain simple, modifying only the geometry of the generated brush.

-----

There's also the problem of `CSGBox` and `CSGCylinder` lacking more geometric options, like subdivisions, shear and trapezoid. It's very difficult to change the mesh generation code without breaking compatibility with projects AND keeping it simple, we would have to keep piling compatibility toggles and options, making it hard to maintain.
For this, I also proposed deprecating these shapes for a new node https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14494 and there were prior proposals to deprecate `CSGBox` and `CSGCylinder` in favor of `CSGPolygon3D` or `CSGMesh3D`. The ability to edit CSGBrushes making a vertex editor also introduces more possibilities in this regard, a CSGBox could be turned into a cylinder or a CSGCylinder into a Box.

@Jesusemora 
> While this was the original idea with #115926 it wasn't a good idea. Adding more properties to CSG nodes is limited, the correct solution is to implement a face editor. I abandoned that PR because I started working on something that would be better at solving the problem, the ability to edit `CSGBrush`es and the possibility of making a face editor #118630

I saw your face editing PR after making this one, but haven’t had a chance to look at it in depth yet. I also have plans for adding per-face configuration and modifiers (probably scriptable, would be used for subdivision for example), and for a `CSGBrush3D` node and editor that should be very reminiscent of how editing brushes are in Trenchbroom 2.

I decided to make this PR anyway because it is a fairly small change. People would be able to use these UV changes while we continue working on larger features like direct face and brush editing, which usually require more testing and review.
